:::{#def-cross-entropy}
#### Cross-entropy

Let $p$ and $q$ be [probability mass functions](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf)
on the same finite set of outcomes $\set{1, \ldots, K}$,
with $p_k$ and $q_k$ the probabilities of outcome $k$.
The **cross-entropy** of $q$ relative to $p$
[@wikipedia_cross_entropy]
is

$$\crossentropyf{p}{q} \eqdef -\sumto{k}{K} p_k \log q_k.$$

We take $-\log 0 = \infty$, so when $q_k = 0$ for an outcome with $p_k > 0$, the cross-entropy is infinite.
A term with $p_k = 0$ is taken to be $0$ whatever $q_k$ is, as for [entropy](#def-entropy).

:::

:::{#def-kl-divergence}
#### Kullback--Leibler divergence (KL divergence, relative entropy)

For $p$ and $q$ as in @def-cross-entropy,
the **Kullback--Leibler divergence** (**KL divergence**, or **relative entropy**)
of $q$ from $p$ is

$$\kldivf{p}{q} \eqdef \sumto{k}{K} p_k \log \frac{p_k}{q_k} = \crossentropyf{p}{q} - \crossentropyf{p}{p}.$$

:::

::: {#rem-kl-asymmetric}
#### The divergence is not symmetric

In general, $\kldivf{p}{q} \ne \kldivf{q}{p}$,
so it is not a distance between $p$ and $q$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-cross-entropy}
#### Cross-entropy and divergence for two coins

Let $p = (\tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{1}{2})$ be a fair coin
and $q = (\tfrac{1}{4}, \tfrac{3}{4})$ a coin biased toward the second outcome.
Using logarithms to base 2, $\log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} = -2$
and $\log_2 \tfrac{3}{4} = \log_2 3 - 2$, so

$$
\ba
\crossentropyf{p}{q} &= -\tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} - \tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{3}{4} \\
&= 1 + \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{2 - \log_2 3} \\
&= 2 - \tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 3 \\
&\approx 1.208, \\
\crossentropyf{p}{p} &= -\tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} \\
&= 1, \\
\kldivf{p}{q} &= \crossentropyf{p}{q} - \crossentropyf{p}{p} = 1 - \tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 3 \approx 0.208.
\ea
$$

Here the cross-entropy is larger than the entropy of $p$,
and the divergence is the difference.

:::

::: {#rem-cross-entropy-source}
#### Where the definitions come from

@murphy2012mlpp [section 2.8.2, pp. 57--58] defines the KL divergence
and the cross-entropy as above,
and gives the coding interpretation:
the cross-entropy is the average number of bits needed
to encode data from a source with distribution $p$
using a code designed for $q$.

:::
